Michael Dobson: Introduction, Portraiture and Frontispieces

 

Fig. 1 John Philip Kemble (1757-1823) in Hamlet, from the painting by Sir Thomas Lawrence (1801), now in Tate Britain

Fig. 2 John Philip Kemble, after a drawing by Sir Thomas Lawrence

Fig. 3 William Creswick (1813-1888), actor-manager of the Surrey Theatre from 1849 to 1862, as Coriolanus, 1851

Fig. 4 Thomas Potter Cooke (1786-1864) in Edward Fitzball's nautical burletta The Pilot (adapted from James Fenimore Cooper's 1824 novel), 1828

Fig. 5 Eliza O'Neill (1791-1872), the leading tragedienne in London from 1815 to 1819, as Belvidera in Thomas Otway's Venice Preserv'd (1827)

Fig. 6 The singer and actress Catherine ‘Kitty' Stephens (1794-1882) in 1818, when she was Covent Garden's leading diva and William Hazlitt's favourite Polly in The Beggar's Opera

Fig. 7 Miss Edmiston (b. 1801), famous for her performances as Jane Shore at Drury Lane, in 1822, shortly before her move to the Surrey

Fig. 8 Mary Amelia Warner (1804-1854), co-manager with Samuel Phelps of Sadlers' Wells from 1844, as Hermione, 1851

Fig. 9 Winifred Emery (1861-1924), Ellen Terry's understudy at the Lyceum and Wilde's original Lady Windermere at the St. James's, in J. M. Barrie's The Little Minister, 1898

Fig. 10 Frontispiece to Benjamin Thompson's translation of Kotzebue's The Stranger, from vol. 23 of The British Theatre (1808)

Fig. 11 Frontispiece to Elizabeth Inchbald's Such Things Are, from vol 23. of The British Theatre (1808)

Fig. 12 Frontispiece to Elizabeth Inchbald's translation of Kotzebue's Lovers' Vows, from vol. 23 of The British Theatre (1808)

Fig. 13 Sybil Crutchley in the Guards' Burlesque production of Dr Faust and Miss Marguerite; or, The Young Duck and the Old Quack, c.1890

Fig. 14 Charles Nugent in the Guards' Burlesque production of Dr Faust and Miss Marguerite; or, The Young Duck and the Old Quack, c.1890
